note: Every threshold cites its source. NASA-STD-3001 sets monitoring duties, sleep, behavioural-health, temperature and CO2 limits but gives no numeric blood-pressure, heart-rate or glucose limits (Vol 1 Rev C, Table E.2-2 lists the conditions only), so those numbers come from named terrestrial guidelines and are labelled as such. 'Project-defined' means the team chose it. Decision support, not a medical device.

redflags.text: Systolic pressure of 180 or more is a hypertensive crisis level.
redflags.source: ACC/AHA 2017 adult blood pressure guideline (terrestrial; NASA-STD-3001 gives no BP numbers)

redflags.text: Systolic pressure under 80 is too low. Lie down with your legs raised and call the crew medical officer.
redflags.source: Project-defined red limit below the NHLBI hypotension line of 90 mmHg

clinical.source: ACC/AHA 2017 adult blood pressure guideline (terrestrial; NASA-STD-3001 gives no BP numbers); lower bound: Hypotension under 90/60 mmHg, NIH NHLBI 'Low Blood Pressure' (terrestrial); spaceflight relevance: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C Table E.2-2, gravity-transition orthostatic intolerance

redflags.text: Diastolic pressure of 120 or more is a hypertensive crisis level.
redflags.source: ACC/AHA 2017 adult blood pressure guideline (terrestrial; NASA-STD-3001 gives no BP numbers)

redflags.text: Diastolic pressure under 40 is too low. Lie down with your legs raised and call the crew medical officer.
redflags.source: Project-defined red limit below the NHLBI hypotension line of 60 mmHg

clinical.source: ACC/AHA 2017 adult blood pressure guideline (terrestrial; NASA-STD-3001 gives no BP numbers); lower bound: Hypotension under 90/60 mmHg, NIH NHLBI 'Low Blood Pressure' (terrestrial); spaceflight relevance: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C Table E.2-2, gravity-transition orthostatic intolerance

redflags.text: A resting heart rate under 40 needs help now.
redflags.source: Project-defined red limit (common clinical convention for urgent bradycardia/tachycardia at rest)

redflags.text: A resting heart rate over 130 needs help now.
redflags.source: Project-defined red limit (common clinical convention for urgent bradycardia/tachycardia at rest)

clinical.source: Adult resting heart rate 60-100 bpm, AHA patient guidance (terrestrial; NASA-STD-3001 gives no HR numbers)

personal.clearsNote: Athletic resting heart rate: 50-59 bpm inside your own learned normal is green. Below 50 is never cleared; red flags (< 40) are never cleared. Team decision, to be reviewed by a flight surgeon.

redflags.text: Blood sugar under 54 mg/dL is clinically significant low sugar.
redflags.source: ADA Standards of Care: level 2 hypoglycaemia, under 54 mg/dL (terrestrial)

redflags.text: Blood sugar of 250 mg/dL or more needs help now.

clinical.source: ADA Standards of Care: fasting glucose 70-99 mg/dL (terrestrial). After a meal, use the 'After a meal' tag (under 140 mg/dL at 2 h).

redflags.text: A temperature of 39.5 °C or more is a high fever.
A temperature under 35.0 °C is too cold for the body.
redflags.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C Appendix C: hypothermia below 35 °C

clinical.source: AASM/SRS adult consensus: 7 h or more (terrestrial). NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C [V1 6001] plans an 8.5 h sleep period.
Project-defined 1-5 self-rating; NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C [V1 4011] requires behavioural health to be monitored within clinically accepted values

redflags.text: A capillary refill time of 4.5 seconds or more needs help now.
redflags.source: Project-defined red limit; delayed capillary refill is a recognised bedside sign of poor peripheral perfusion. Experimental phone-camera measurement, not validated.

clinical.source: Bedside convention: capillary refill under about 3 s is usually normal in adults at room temperature. Experimental, not validated.

symptoms.source: Project-defined, based on standard emergency warning signs

meal.label: After a meal
meal.source: ADA: under 140 mg/dL 2 h after eating (terrestrial)

TR-SLEEP-3.source: Project-defined; NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C [V1 6001] plans 8.5 h of sleep

TR-MOOD-3.source: Project-defined; NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C [V1 4011], [V1 6010] private psychological conference

PT-FATIGUE.label: Fatigue pattern
PT-FATIGUE.source: Project-defined; NASA HRP risk: Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization and Work Overload

PT-FEVER.label: Possible infection
PT-FEVER.source: Project-defined; fever 38.0 °C or more with raised heart rate

PT-ORTHO.label: Light-headed on standing
PT-ORTHO.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C Table E.2-2: gravity-transition orthostatic intolerance; project-defined trigger

repeatYellow.source: Project-defined: yellow on 3 of the last 5 days

replyClock.note: Inputs to the Earth Reply Clock. Light time and Sun blackout are real (NASA JPL Horizons). Shift hours, response times, contact windows and act-by windows are project-defined assumptions, shown on screen as such.
replyClock.actSource: Project-defined act-by windows: red = first-response window; patterns = their recheck time; yellow = before the next check.

surgeon.label: Flight surgeon on console 07:00-19:00 Houston (UTC-6)
surgeon.source: Project-defined assumption. Off shift, a red alert pages the on-call surgeon; routine messages wait for the next shift.

contact.source: Project-defined: continuous relay by default; optional 8 h contact window per sol

replyClock.concept: NASA Earth-Independent Medical Operations (EIMO) concept of operations, NTRS 20250000009: decisions move to the crew when the ground is communication-delayed beyond practicality.
